proposed.text: Architect C's architectural drawings and design images were copied to a project website without permission and remain online. The unauthorized use began five years before discovery. What remedy framing is most source-safe under RA 8293?

options.text: The architect must accept the use because any online infringement older than three years eliminates all remedies
The architect may seek an injunction to stop continuing infringement and may seek damages subject to RA 8293 proof and timing rules
The architect can only demand removal because monetary remedies are never available for online publication
All legal action is barred once the use has continued for five years, even if the material remains online

rationale.a: This overstates the time issue; RA 8293 has a damages limit, not a blanket rule that erases every possible remedy.
rationale.c: Section 216 includes monetary remedies; removal is not the only civil remedy.
rationale.d: This treats the four-year damages limit as a total bar to all relief, which the local source does not support.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 177 protects economic rights such as reproduction, public display, and communication to the public. Section 216 allows injunction and damages/profits remedies. Section 226 limits damages recovery after four years from the time the cause of action arose, so the source-safe answer preserves prospective relief and treats damages as timing- and proof-dependent.
rationale.takeaway: Long-running unauthorized use requires a remedies analysis: injunction may stop continuing infringement, while damages are subject to RA 8293 limits.

proposed.explanation: Source-audited against RA 8293 Sections 177, 216, and 226; revised to avoid an unlimited damages claim after five years.
